options: голос
голоса
голосу
голосом
cases.translation: From there a voice unfamiliar to Levin could be heard.
cases.explain: Голос is the subject of слышался (was heard), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Мальчика, которого он взял из ___, чтобы воспитывать, он в припадке злости так избил, что началось дело.
options: деревня
деревни
деревню
деревней
cases.translation: The boy whom he had taken from the village to raise, he beat so badly in a fit of anger that a case was opened.
cases.explain: The preposition из (from, out of) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Левин подошел к ___, прочел адрес брата, который у него был в бумажнике.
options: фонарь
фонаря
фонарю
фонарём
cases.translation: Levin went up to a streetlamp and read his brother's address, which he had in his wallet.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward, up to) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Он прочел адрес брата и подозвал ___.
options: извозчик
извозчика
извозчику
извозчиком
cases.translation: He read his brother's address and hailed a cabman.
cases.explain: Извозчика is the direct object of the transitive verb подозвал (hailed/called over), so it is accusative.

options: учитель
учителя
учителю
учителем
cases.translation: He took a position at the public school as a teacher.
cases.explain: Учителем is a predicate instrumental, expressing the role he took on (поступил кем — became/served as a teacher).

cases.sentence: Вспоминал он, как брат в ___ и год после университета жил как монах.
options: университет
университета
университету
университете
cases.translation: He recalled how his brother, at the university and for a year after, had lived like a monk.
cases.explain: The preposition в (at, in) indicating location governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: «Да что-то есть во мне противное, отталкивающее», — думал Левин, вышедший от Щербацких и пешком направляясь к брату.
reading.question: What did Levin think about himself as he walked from the Shcherbatskys' toward his brother's?
options: That there was something repulsive and off-putting about him
That he was the most eligible man in Moscow
That Kitty had misunderstood him completely
That he needed new clothes for the next ball
reading.correct: That there was something repulsive and off-putting about him
reading.explain: Levin thought there was 'something repulsive, repellent' in himself, walking away from the Shcherbatskys toward his brother.

reading.ru: Какое право имел я думать, что она захочет соединить свою жизнь с моею?
reading.question: What does Levin question about his hopes regarding Kitty?
options: What right he had to think she would want to join her life with his
Whether Kitty was even old enough to marry
Whether her parents approved of him
Whether Vronsky was a better match financially
reading.correct: What right he had to think she would want to join her life with his
reading.explain: Levin asks himself what right he had to think she would want to unite her life with his.

reading.ru: И едва ли мы справедливо судим и судили о брате Николае?
reading.question: What does Levin begin to doubt about how their brother Nikolai is judged?
options: Whether he and others have judged Nikolai fairly
Whether Nikolai is actually still alive
Whether Nikolai ever attended university
Whether Nikolai has more money than believed
reading.correct: Whether he and others have judged Nikolai fairly
reading.explain: Levin wonders whether he and others have judged, and are judging, their brother Nikolai fairly.

reading.ru: Левин подошел к фонарю, прочел адрес брата, который у него был в бумажнике, и подозвал извозчика.
reading.question: What did Levin do to find his brother's address?
options: He went to a streetlamp and read the address from his wallet
He asked a policeman for directions
He remembered it from a previous visit
He sent a telegram asking for the address
reading.correct: He went to a streetlamp and read the address from his wallet
reading.explain: Levin walked up to a streetlamp, read his brother's address which he had in his wallet, and hailed a cab.

reading.ru: И потом, как вдруг его прорвало, он сблизился с самыми гадкими людьми и пустился в самый беспутный разгул».
reading.question: What happened to Nikolai after his period of strict religious devotion suddenly broke?
options: He grew close to the most vile people and threw himself into wild dissipation
He became even more devout and joined a monastery
He left Russia to travel abroad
He reconciled with his family completely
reading.correct: He grew close to the most vile people and threw himself into wild dissipation
reading.explain: The text says that after it suddenly 'burst' in him, Nikolai grew close to the vilest people and plunged into the most reckless dissipation.

reading.ru: Вспоминал затеянный им постыдный процесс с братом Сергеем Ивановичем за то, что тот будто бы не выплатил ему долю из материнского имения.
reading.question: What lawsuit did Nikolai bring against their brother Sergei Ivanovich?
options: A shameful suit claiming Sergei hadn't paid him his share of their mother's estate
A suit over a stolen horse
A suit about unpaid gambling debts between them
A suit to inherit their father's title
reading.correct: A shameful suit claiming Sergei hadn't paid him his share of their mother's estate
reading.explain: Levin recalled the shameful lawsuit Nikolai started against their brother Sergei Ivanovich, claiming he had not paid out his share of their mother's estate.

reading.ru: Его дразнили, звали его Ноем, монахом, а когда его прорвало, никто не помог ему, а все с ужасом и омерзением отвернулись».
reading.question: How did people treat Nikolai during his devout period, and then after his breakdown?
options: They mocked him as 'Noah' and a monk, then turned away in horror and disgust once he broke down
They respected him deeply throughout both periods
They ignored him entirely during his devout period only
They supported him financially through his crisis
reading.correct: They mocked him as 'Noah' and a monk, then turned away in horror and disgust once he broke down
reading.explain: They teased him, calling him Noah and a monk, and when he broke down, no one helped him — everyone turned away in horror and disgust.

reading.ru: «Наверху двенадцатый и тринадцатый», — ответил швейцар на вопрос Левина.
reading.question: What information did the doorman give Levin about his brother's room?
options: That rooms twelve and thirteen were upstairs
That his brother had already checked out
That no one by that name was staying there
That his brother was out for the evening
reading.correct: That rooms twelve and thirteen were upstairs
reading.explain: The doorman answered Levin's question by saying rooms twelve and thirteen were upstairs.

reading.ru: Константин Левин заглянул в дверь и увидел, что говорит с огромной шапкой волос молодой человек в поддевке, а молодая рябоватая женщина в шерстяном платье, без рукавчиков и воротничков сидит на диване.
reading.question: What did Levin see when he peeked through the door of his brother's room?
options: A young man with a huge shock of hair talking, and a pockmarked young woman sitting on the sofa
His brother alone, reading quietly
An empty room with no one present
Several police officers questioning someone
reading.correct: A young man with a huge shock of hair talking, and a pockmarked young woman sitting on the sofa
reading.explain: Levin saw a young man with a great shock of hair, in a peasant coat, talking, and a young pockmarked woman in a woolen dress sitting on the sofa.

reading.ru: Женщина встала, вышла за перегородку и увидала Константина.
reading.question: What did the woman do that led her to notice Konstantin at the door?
options: She got up, went behind the partition, and saw him
She opened a window and called out
She fell asleep on the sofa
She left the room entirely without noticing him
reading.correct: She got up, went behind the partition, and saw him
reading.explain: The woman stood up, went out behind the partition, and that is when she saw Konstantin.

reading.ru: «Кто я?» — еще сердитее повторил голос Николая.
reading.question: How did Nikolai react when told 'someone' was asking for him?
options: He angrily repeated 'Who am I?' even more irritated
He calmly asked the visitor to wait
He immediately recognized his brother's voice
He refused to respond at all
reading.correct: He angrily repeated 'Who am I?' even more irritated
reading.explain: Nikolai's voice repeated 'Who am I?' even more angrily than before.

reading.ru: Волосы стали реже, те же прямые усы висели на губы, те же глаза странно и наивно смотрели на вошедшего.
reading.question: What had changed and what had stayed the same about Nikolai's appearance?
options: His hair had thinned, but his mustache and strangely naive eyes remained the same
He had grown a full beard and looked completely different
His eyes had changed color entirely
He had gained a significant amount of weight
reading.correct: His hair had thinned, but his mustache and strangely naive eyes remained the same
reading.explain: His hair had become thinner, but the same straight mustache hung over his lips, and the same eyes looked strangely and naively at the newcomer.

reading.ru: «Я писал и вам, и Сергею Ивановичу, что я вас не знаю и не хочу знать.
reading.question: What had Nikolai written to both Konstantin and Sergei Ivanovich?
options: That he didn't know them and didn't want to know them
That he needed money urgently
That he was moving abroad permanently
That he forgave them for past wrongs
reading.correct: That he didn't know them and didn't want to know them
reading.explain: Nikolai says he wrote to both of them that he did not know them and did not want to know them.

reading.question: What effect did Konstantin's timidity have on Nikolai?
options: It visibly softened Nikolai
It made Nikolai angrier
It had no visible effect at all
It made Nikolai leave the room
reading.explain: The text says his brother's timidity evidently softened Nikolai.

reading.ru: И он оглянулся по своей привычке на всех бывших в комнате.
reading.question: What habitual gesture did Nikolai make while speaking?
options: He glanced around at everyone in the room, as was his habit
He tapped his foot nervously
He covered his mouth when speaking
He stood up and paced
reading.correct: He glanced around at everyone in the room, as was his habit
reading.explain: As was his habit, he glanced around at everyone present in the room.

reading.ru: «Да, Киевского был», — насупившись сердито говорил Крицкий.
reading.question: How did Kritsky respond when asked if he was from Kiev University?
options: He confirmed it, scowling angrily as he spoke
He denied it and named another university
He laughed and joked about it
He refused to answer the question
reading.correct: He confirmed it, scowling angrily as he spoke
reading.explain: Kritsky answered 'Yes, I was at Kiev,' frowning and speaking angrily.

reading.ru: «Но люблю ее и уважаю и всех, кто меня хочет знать», прибавил он, возвышая голос и хмурясь.
reading.question: How does Nikolai describe his feelings toward Marya Nikolaevna and those who accept him?
options: He says he loves and respects her, and everyone who wants to know him
He says he merely tolerates her presence
He says he is ashamed of her
He says he plans to leave her soon
reading.correct: He says he loves and respects her, and everyone who wants to know him
reading.explain: Nikolai adds, raising his voice and frowning, that he loves and respects her, and everyone who wants to know him.
